Meet Senator Keefer
Dawn Keefer has been a champion of right-sizing government and reining in government regulation during her time in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives from 2017-2024, and since her election to the state Senate in November 2024. As State Representative of the 92nd legislative district in Northern York County, Keefer cut her legislative teeth during her first year in office, developing a non-taxing solution to balance a state budget that included $1.5 billion more in spending than in projected revenues.

My School Property Tax Plan Includes Stronger Accountability
School property taxes remain the number one issue I hear about from my constituents, particularly seniors and homeowners living on fixed incomes who face higher bills year after year. My
School Property Tax Elimination Act, Senate Bill 962
, is designed to address that burden while also providing a more sustainable approach to funding public education, including addressing funding challenges in lower socioeconomic districts.
The legislation also includes stronger accountability measures for school districts. Each district would be required to balance its budget annually. If a district fails to do so, it would have one year, with the assistance of an appointed adviser, to return to a balanced budget. If the district remains unable to balance its budget after that period, it would be dissolved and merged with another district. This approach is intended to encourage responsible financial management and help prevent districts with declining enrollment from maintaining unnecessary staffing and administrative costs.
I’ll be discussing the proposal at my next School Property Tax Elimination Town Hall on Wednesday, Oct. 14, from 6-8 p.m. at New Castle School of Trades, 4117 Pulaski Road, New Castle. Life Is a Gift: Speaking at the March for Life
More than 6,000 Pennsylvanians gathered at the state Capitol for the largest Pennsylvania March for Life to date, coming together from communities across the commonwealth to stand for the protection of unborn children. Life is a gift, and every life has inherent value and dignity.
I was proud to speak at the rally
and shared a clear message for all Pennsylvanians and elected officials: “Protect the unborn. Support mothers. Reject efforts to expand abortion access at the expense of our most vulnerable, and never forget that the right to life is the foundation of every other right.”
I will continue to be a voice for those who cannot speak for themselves and advocate for policies that recognize the value of every human life.
Shapiro’s Troubling Health Regulations: Thousands of Pennsylvanians Weigh In
Thousands of Pennsylvanians — including ordinary citizens, school officials and many others — spoke out against Gov. Josh Shapiro’s proposed health regulations, and their voices were heard. Following strong public opposition, the Pennsylvania Department of Health withdrew the proposed regulations on Sept. 25. More than 10,000 public comments were submitted opposing the changes.
I added my voice to the effort through an
individual letter to the Independent Regulatory Review Commission
, as well as a
joint letter signed by members of the Senate Republican Caucus
, outlining the reasons these regulations must be stopped. Thank you to everyone who took the time to learn about the proposal, submitted a comment and made your voice heard.
This is a win for Pennsylvanians today and a reminder of what can happen when people pay attention, speak up and refuse to sit on the sidelines. But this is not the last you’ll see of this issue. The administration plans to resubmit a revised proposal, so I’ll be watching closely to see what comes next and will continue standing up for the rights and freedoms of Pennsylvanians.

State Health Regulations information webpage
.

It was great to see that mission in action right here in our community — and I even found a few treasures along the way!

The right skills can provide more than a job — they can provide an opportunity to build a career and support a family.
Empire Beauty School in York is helping students take that step

My visit also connected with legislation I introduced, Senate Bill 892
, which would remove unnecessary government barriers for professionals with limited scopes of practice. By reducing these barriers, we can create more opportunities for individuals to enter the workforce, earn an income and put their skills to good use.
I appreciated the opportunity to learn more about how Empire is preparing students to enter the workforce and support our local economy.

9/11: 25 Years Later
This year marks 25 years since the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks that claimed nearly 3,000 innocent lives and forever changed our nation. Four commercial airliners were hijacked and used as weapons of terror. Two were flown into the World Trade Center towers in New York City, another struck the Pentagon, and the fourth crashed in Somerset County after brave passengers fought back against the hijackers.
Twenty-five years later, the shock and grief of that day remain deeply felt. But so does the courage of the first responders, the passengers of Flight 93 and countless others who stepped forward in the face of unimaginable danger. Remembering the Sacrifice of Korean War Veterans
Korean War Armistice Day serves as an important reminder of the courage and sacrifice of the more than 1.7 million Americans who served during the Korean War. This past week, I was grateful for the opportunity to attend the 73rd Commemoration Anniversary of the Korean War Armistice at the
Shiloh American Legion 791
in Dover, where I joined Korean War veterans, members of the Korean American community and local leaders in honoring those who served.
The event provided a meaningful opportunity to recognize the bravery and dedication of these veterans and reflect on the lasting impact of their service in defending freedom. Their sacrifices should never be forgotten.
Springettsbury Township Park to Host Special Concert Honoring Veterans
Music and patriotism will take center stage Saturday, Aug. 15, at
Springettsbury Township Park
as the community comes together to show appreciation for our nation’s veterans and celebrate America’s 250th year.
The Springettsbury Township Park Amphitheater, 1501 Mt. Zion Road, York, will host the
United States Air Force Heritage of America Band
from 7 – 8:30 p.m. The seven-member popular music ensemble will perform a variety of genres, including rock, pop, country and R&B. The concert is free and open to the community.
This special concert is a wonderful opportunity to enjoy live music while coming together as a community to recognize the service and sacrifice of our veterans and celebrate 250 years of American history.
Salute to Service Night at WellSpan Park
Service members and veterans are invited to
Salute to Service Night with the York Revolution
on Wednesday, Aug. 19, at 6:30 p.m. at WellSpan Park. It’s a great opportunity to enjoy an evening of baseball while being recognized and celebrated for your service to our country.
Service members and veterans can receive a free game ticket and food voucher, with food vouchers available for pickup at the ticket office Will Call window on game day. Additional family members can join in the fun with discounted $10 tickets.
When purchasing tickets, add the total number of tickets to your cart and use the discount drop-down option beside each ticket to designate service member tickets as free.
New Law Connects Families of Deceased Services Members with Support
In an effort to better connect families with their local veterans affairs office, the General Assembly unanimously passed
Senate Bill 130
, now Act 42 of 2026, which requires funeral directors and cemeteries to provide the family of a deceased serviceperson contact information for the county director of veterans affairs. They must also notify the county director of veterans affairs of the death of a service person within 96 hours of receiving their remains.
Pennsylvania county veterans affairs offices are available to better assist veterans access benefits for which they might be eligible, and
their contact information can be found here
.
Honoring Veterans with Visual Impairments with a Capitol Monument
A Braille Flag monument honoring veterans with visual impairments could be installed at the Pennsylvania Capitol Building under legislation passed by the Senate and sent to the House of Representatives for consideration.
The Braille Flag was created to honor the service of veterans who have been left with life-long visual disabilities. Under
Senate Bill 1303
, the monument would be made of bronze and include the Pledge of Allegiance in Braille.
The display would be sponsored by the Moose Lodge and the American Braille Flag Project, a non-profit organization dedicated to the placement of these flags throughout the country.
Read more about Senate Bill 1303 here

The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs’
Homeless Aging and Disabled Veterans Initiative
aims to help homeless veterans with chronic, complex health needs secure affordable housing within their communities or transition more easily to any higher levels of care they need. The initiative works to better integrate home and community healthcare, social services and permanent supportive housing.
